historical_reviews.deepseek: Correctly distinguishes enumeration from traffic, but logging into the DUT host and listing USB tty nodes may see a host adapter rather than the HMC UART, and the command is insecure/malformed.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Adds HMC controller/access ownership, exact USB-C/tty topology, operator loopback/peer, full logs, byte/error criteria and recovery.
historical_reviews.v3_1: The HMC subject requires explicit ownership rather than an inferred host device; ED-01/03 require two-way traffic, ED-07/08 bind the path, ED-11/12 forbid unsafe retry, and ED-36/38 reserve verdict ownership.

original_test_intent: Prove the HMC's UART is physically routed to the named USB-C connector and carries clean bidirectional traffic through the correct HMC console/device path, rather than accepting an unrelated host USB-serial enumeration.
original_method: Establish whether HMC is independently accessible or proxied and map its UART controller/channel through connector/cable/adapter to a stable HMC-owned tty or console endpoint; document service/console ownership and an independent recovery path; have an operator attach the approved USB-C peer/loopback; configure the exact serial profile; exchange a bounded framed payload in both directions; compare content/order/count/timeouts and HMC UART errors; close the endpoint and restore its prior ownership without host-device substitution, console commands, HMC reset or automatic retry.
manual_activity: An operator identifies and photographs the HMC-to-USB-C connector/cable/adapter, attaches the approved isolated loopback or peer, and maintains a separate recovery channel while the HMC UART is exercised.
required_inputs: HMC native or documented proxy access and HMC UART controller/channel-to-USB-C/adapter/endpoint map
Stable HMC endpoint identity plus current console/getty/debug ownership and independent recovery
Baud/data/parity/stop/flow profile, peer/loopback, bounded payload/directions, timeout and error limits
Operator procedure, cleanup and HMC recovery without reset or host substitution
safety_requirements: Prove the endpoint belongs to the HMC path; do not treat a host ttyACM/ttyUSB node as HMC evidence without architecture mapping
Confirm the UART is not the sole HMC control/recovery console and keep an independent management route
Use non-sensitive bounded framed traffic; avoid shell/control escape sequences, credentials and uncontrolled echo loops
Do not stop console services, change firmware/boot configuration, reset HMC/USB/UART or clear logs to retry
Stop on wrong-owner response, prompt/debug interaction, HMC management degradation, serial errors or disconnect; no automatic retry
agent_execution_scope: Validate HMC access/ownership, UART-to-USB-C topology, stable endpoint, service ownership, peer and serial contract
Collect full HMC/USB/serial baseline and, after operator setup, run the approved bounded bidirectional exchange
Verify exact bytes/order/count, timeouts, error deltas and uninterrupted HMC management, then restore endpoint ownership
Do not infer HMC from host enumeration, use insecure access, write an unknown console, reset HMC state or issue the DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve HMC-native/proxy access and exact UART/channel/USB-C/adapter/endpoint mapping
Approve console/service ownership, independent recovery, peer, serial profile, payload and error/timeout limits
Review HMC-bound physical and traffic evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Host `ttyACM*`/`ttyUSB*` and dmesg output may identify an adapter but do not prove it is the HMC UART; the shown SSH command is malformed, insecure and truncated.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the authoritative HMC-native or documented proxy endpoint, preserve complete topology/ownership logs, and exchange the approved framed payload with the operator-confirmed USB-C peer while monitoring HMC health.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: HMC-to-USB-C bidirectional UART scope and 20/20-minute allocation remain; HMC access, endpoint, serial settings and peer are not inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: First prove HMC ownership of the controller and endpoint, then execute two-direction framed traffic over the physical USB-C path with byte/error accounting and independent recovery.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds HMC/host disambiguation, stable endpoint mapping, management protection, actual traffic criteria and restoration.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A host USB serial adapter can enumerate even when the HMC UART is unmapped or inactive; the same device node may also expose a different console path.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Writing an HMC control console or losing the only HMC access path can disrupt platform management and make recovery dependent on physical service.

project_override_considerations: A host-visible USB tty is valid only when the approved topology proves it is the endpoint of the HMC UART and bidirectional traffic traverses the named USB-C route. Enumeration alone is insufficient.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash, authorization and HMC-native/proxy ownership diagram
HMC UART/channel-to-USB-C/adapter/stable endpoint map and operator connection photo
Complete endpoint service/console ownership, USB descriptors, driver and HMC/serial logs
Exact serial profile and timestamped two-way framed payload with byte/order/count, timeout and error comparisons
Independent HMC management health plus restored closed/original endpoint state

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require HMC-to-USB-C bidirectional UART function. The host-side assumption is confined to the reference method.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The HMC UART objective is clear. Access/ownership mapping, physical peer, serial contract and recovery are supplyable prerequisites.

review_improvement: Prevents host USB enumeration from falsely passing an HMC-owned UART case and requires end-to-end HMC-bound traffic with management-path protection.
independent_technical_reasoning: The named source is HMC, yet the reference logs into the DUT host. That can only be valid if the architecture shows a USB-serial endpoint representing the HMC UART. Therefore ownership and topology must precede any traffic. The criterion demands both directions, so framed byte comparison is needed; continuous HMC reachability and an independent recovery path are specific safety gates because selecting an HMC console incorrectly can remove platform-management access.
